- Uncovered claim 'Following last year's sales org consolidation, a number of our most valuable Enterprise accounts were left without an assigned account executive for the entire second half of the year.' [PARAMETRIC]: The claim asserts that top-value Enterprise accounts were unowned for the ENTIRE second half of the year (both Q3 and Q4). AC1 measures unowned share only at FY26-Q4, which proves end-of-year ownership but not that the accounts were unowned across the full H2 period. The existing unowned_account_share check CAN express this substance if applied to the earlier quarter(s) of H2; the drafted criteria omit the H2-wide duration dimension, so a dataset where accounts were re-owned by Q3 would pass AC1 yet falsify the claim. (consider check: unowned_account_share)
Drafted 3 criteria: AC1, AC2, AC3
Coverage guard: 1 note(s) - proceeding:

[note] Uncovered claim 'Following last year's sales org consolidation, a number of our most valuable Enterprise accounts were left without an assigned account executive for the entire second half of the year.' [PARAMETRIC]: The claim asserts the unowned condition persisted across the entire second half of the year (H2-wide duration), not merely at a single quarter. AC2 checks only FY26-Q3 at 25% unowned share, which does not fail if the accounts were owned in Q1 or Q2 and only became unowned in Q3. No drafted criterion measures unowned status across both H2 quarters (e.g. Q2 and Q3) simultaneously, so a dataset where accounts were owned for most of H2 but unowned only at year-end would pass. The existing unowned_account_share check CAN express this substance but no criterion applies it to the full H2 window. (consider check: unowned_account_share)

- Uncovered claim 'Following last year's sales org consolidation, a number of our most valuable Enterprise accounts were left without an assigned account executive for the entire second half of the year.' [PARAMETRIC]: The claim asserts unownership persisted for the ENTIRE second half of the year (both Q3 and Q4). AC2 only checks FY26-Q4, which does not prove the accounts were unowned during the first half of the second quarter period as well. A dataset where accounts gained owners in Q3 but lost them again in Q4 would pass AC2 yet fail the 'entire second half' substance. The existing unowned_account_share check CAN express this but the drafted criteria do not cover the full half-year duration. (consider check: unowned_account_share)
Drafted 3 criteria: AC1, AC2, AC3
Coverage guard: 2 note(s) - proceeding:

[note] Uncovered claim 'The consolidation left strategic accounts unowned rather than rebalancing them to remaining coverage.' [VOCAB_GAP]: The claim's substance is a comparative counterfactual: that accounts were left unowned instead of being reassigned to remaining account executives. No existing check can express account reassignment/rebalancing behavior or the absence thereof. The unowned_account_share check measures the state of being unowned but cannot distinguish 'left unowned' from 'rebalanced away,' so no check can prove this claim's substance.

[note] Uncovered claim 'Following last year's sales org consolidation, a number of our most valuable Enterprise accounts were left without an assigned account executive for the entire second half of the year.' [PARAMETRIC]: The claim asserts the accounts were unowned for the ENTIRE second half of the year (both Q3 and Q4). AC1 only checks unowned share at FY26-Q3 and AC2 only at FY26-Q4; neither criterion would fail if the accounts had gained an owner in one of those quarters. Coverage of the 'entire half-year' duration requires a criterion asserting unowned status across both quarters simultaneously, which is not drafted. The existing check CAN express this but the drafted criteria do not. (consider check: unowned_account_share)
